title: Change-free
statementMd:
Student Arseny likes to plan his life for $*n*$ days ahead. He visits a canteen every day and he has already decided what he will order in each of the following $*n*$ days. Prices in the canteen do not change and that means Arseny will spend $*c*_{*i*}$ rubles during the $*i*$-th day.

There are $1$-ruble coins and $100$-ruble notes in circulation. At this moment, Arseny has $*m*$ coins and a sufficiently large amount of notes (you can assume that he has an infinite amount of them). Arseny loves modern technologies, so he uses his credit card everywhere except the canteen, but he has to pay in cash in the canteen because it does not accept cards.

Cashier always asks the student to pay change-free. However, it's not always possible, but Arseny tries to minimize the *dissatisfaction* of the cashier. Cashier's dissatisfaction for each of the days is determined by the total amount of notes and coins in the change. To be precise, if the cashier gives Arseny $*x*$ notes and coins on the $*i*$-th day, his dissatisfaction for this day equals $*x*·*w*_{*i*}$. Cashier always gives change using as little coins and notes as possible, he always has enough of them to be able to do this.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1e73f168321ccf0780d65694cedf31370a08e203.png) "Caution! Angry cashier"

Arseny wants to pay in such a way that the total dissatisfaction of the cashier for $*n*$ days would be as small as possible. Help him to find out how he needs to pay in each of the $*n*$ days!

Note that Arseny always has enough money to pay, because he has an infinite amount of notes. Arseny can use notes and coins he received in change during any of the following days.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$, $0 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9}$) — the amount of days Arseny planned his actions for and the amount of coins he currently has.

The second line contains a sequence of integers $*c*_{1}, *c*_{2}, ..., *c*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$) — the amounts of money in rubles which Arseny is going to spend for each of the following days.

The third line contains a sequence of integers $*w*_{1}, *w*_{2}, ..., *w*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *w*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$) — the cashier's dissatisfaction coefficients for each of the following days.

## Output

In the first line print one integer — minimum possible total dissatisfaction of the cashier.

Then print $*n*$ lines, the $*i*$-th of then should contain two numbers — the amount of notes and the amount of coins which Arseny should use to pay in the canteen on the $*i*$-th day.

Of course, the total amount of money Arseny gives to the casher in any of the days should be no less than the amount of money he has planned to spend. It also shouldn't exceed $10^{6}$ rubles: Arseny never carries large sums of money with him.

If there are multiple answers, print any of them.
statementZhMd:
学生 Arseny 喜欢提前规划好未来 $*n*$ 天的生活。他每天都会去食堂，并且已经决定好了接下来 $*n*$ 天每天要点什么。食堂的价格不会改变，这意味着 Arseny 在第 $*i*$ 天会花费 $*c*_{*i*}$ 卢布。

市面上流通着面值为 $1$ 卢布的硬币和面值为 $100$ 卢布的纸币。目前，Arseny 有 $*m*$ 枚硬币和足够多的纸币（可以认为他拥有无限张纸币）。Arseny 喜欢现代科技，因此除了食堂以外，他在其他地方都使用信用卡，但由于食堂不接受银行卡，他必须在食堂使用现金支付。

收银员总是要求学生恰好付款。然而，这并不总是可能，但 Arseny 会尽量减小收银员的*不满程度*。收银员每天的不满程度由找零中纸币和硬币的总数量决定。准确地说，如果收银员在第 $*i*$ 天找给 Arseny $*x*$ 张纸币和枚硬币，那么当天收银员的不满程度就是 $*x*·*w*_{*i*}$。收银员总是使用尽可能少的硬币和纸币来找零，并且他总是有足够的硬币和纸币来完成找零。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1e73f168321ccf0780d65694cedf31370a08e203.png) "小心！愤怒的收银员"

Arseny 希望通过合理付款，使收银员 $*n*$ 天的不满程度总和尽可能小。请帮助他找出每天应该如何付款！

注意，Arseny 总是有足够的钱付款，因为他拥有无限多的纸币。Arseny 可以在之后的任意一天使用找零中得到的纸币和硬币。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$，$0 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{9}$）——Arseny 计划安排的天数，以及他当前拥有的硬币数量。

第二行包含一列整数 $*c*_{1}, *c*_{2}, ..., *c*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$）——Arseny 接下来每天计划花费的卢布数。

第三行包含一列整数 $*w*_{1}, *w*_{2}, ..., *w*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *w*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$）——接下来每天收银员的不满系数。

## 输出格式

第一行输出一个整数——收银员可能获得的不满程度总和的最小值。

接下来输出 $*n*$ 行，第 $*i*$ 行应包含两个数——Arseny 在第 $*i*$ 天于食堂付款时应使用的纸币数量和硬币数量。

当然，Arseny 在任意一天支付的金额都不能少于他计划花费的金额，也不能超过 $10^{6}$ 卢布：Arseny 从不随身携带大笔现金。

如果有多种答案，输出任意一种即可。
